newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Lung Kee sees 10 pct revenue boost from Guangzhou.
newsitem.headline: Lung Kee sees 10 pct revenue boost from Guangzhou.

text.p: Mould base maker Lung Kee Metal Holdings Ltd expects a 10 percent revenue boost from its new Guangzhou plant, executive director William Wai said on Monday.
"After an initial three to five percent, the Guangzhou plant will boost total revenue by 10 percent after its second year of operations. That's in fiscal 2000," Wai told a news conference.
For the fiscal year ended March 1997, European orders were at HK$2 to HK$3 million, Wai said.

The Guangzhou plant, now under construction, is due to start production in early 1998. Output from the plant is targetted at the European market, which requires a different product standard from Asia, he said.
Wai said he was confident Lung Kee would be able to make a mark in the already mature European market due to the group's lower production costs.
"The future of the European market is quite good and our costs are lower than the European manufacturers," Wai said, declining to indicate the exact figures.
He said the sale price of European standard mould bases were double those of Asian standards and the European market was more than double the size of the Hong Kong and Guangzhou markets put together.
Wai said Lung Kee's Shanghai plant, which has a capacity to produce 1,000 mould sets per month, started operations in July and was expected to boost the group's total capacity by 10 percent.
The group has production facilities in China, Malaysia, Hong Kong and Singapore.

Plans to start building a 150 sets per month capacity Malaysian plant in July have been delayed by nine months because the property developer had not yet handed over the site. "We can expect to receive the site by third quarter of September," Wai said. "The plant should be operational in April-May 1998."
To meet the Malaysian demand, the group is renting a 30 sets per month capacity factory.
The group is looking at setting up new plants in northern and western China as well as India. Wai said.
"Our aim is to become number one in Asia," Wai said.
Among the group's competitors are Japan's Futaba Corp in Asia and Hasco Steel Co in Europe.
